Tech companies regularly file for patents that they don’t end up actually putting into real products, but this one, called “creating a channel of video experiences tailored to a user,” describes a system that many AI companies have been clearly trying to build. It imagines something called “My Channel,” which would be filled with AI content generated based on demographic data, their video watch history (presumably from YouTube), and other information it knows about the user. It would then make “the user as the protagonist for the whole video.” The patent was first noticed by Patentlyze , a news site that tracks tech company patents, who shared it with 404 Media. “You are a customized video generating model. Generate a customized video for a user where the user will play the protagonist,” a hypothetical LLM prompt in the patent reads. “The generated customized video includes characteristics based on the <user_profile>. The generated customized video follows the style and format of the <top_ watches> of the user. The generated customized video sticks to the <preferred_genres> of the user but the narrative for the generated customized video is customized. The <top watches> and <preferred _genres> parameters are ordered from more preferred to less preferred.” It suggests that the channel would be connected to an “advertising server,” and that advertisements would be inserted into the customized AI content: “an advertising stitcher included in the advertising server generates an updated customized media content item by inserting at least one advertisement into the customized media content item,” it says. The patent imagines, for example, “a crime/comedy caper,” “a fun romantic comedy,” “a sci-fi adventure,” and “an action/thriller experience” with a viewer named “John” as the protagonist. Another prompt included in the patent suggests that someone who had recently watched cricket highlights of a “Player 1” might then be served a similar video “that incorporates elements of the Cricket World Cup and Player 1’s recent performance. Perhaps [user_name] could be cheering for India in the stands or interacting with Player 1 in some way.” The notable thing about this patent is that it is barely an evolution of what is already happening on social media and what is beginning to happen on streaming free TV channels on services like Samsung TV Plus and TCLtv+. The people generating AI slop on social media are making incredibly specific content because they know that social media algorithms will be highly effective at filtering people there . Meta is already allowing advertisers to use AI to generate many slightly different versions of an advertisement; its targeting AI then automatically shows them to users who are most likely to react to a specific version of an ad. As I’ve previously reported, TCL has been experimenting with AI-generated content on its streaming free TV channels, and, even without AI-generated content, free streaming TV channels have gotten incredibly specific. It is now possible, for example, to watch reruns of individual shows 24/7/365. AI boosters have long been saying the future of entertainment is allowing anyone to generate their own TV shows, or to generate “new” episodes of existing properties. An always-on, autogenerating, customized AI TV channel isn’t far off from that idea. As I’ve previously argued, the future that tech companies envision is one in which we are somehow even more siloed than we are now. They imagine a world in which everyone lives in their own reality and watches their own, customized content, which is a world in which big, unifying pieces of media are harder to make and are few and far between. The Google patent comes on the heels of a Microsoft patent that describes a system that alters spoken words (and the person’s lips) in live video, thereby distorting reality.

Introducing Muse in the UK: A Personal AI Agent You Control
Muse is now in the UK: a personal AI agent that doesn't just answer questions, but one that you can task to get things done on your behalf From doing the Christmas shopping and searching for a cheaper energy deal, to sorting the school calendar or turning your saved travel Reels into a holiday itinerary, Muse can get it done for you. And from today, Meta’s personal AI agent, which proactively helps with your goals and suggests ideas, is available in the UK. It’s simple to use. Chat with Muse in the app or directly in WhatsApp, tell it what it needs to get done, check its output, and it takes action. Powered by Muse Spark – the first model from Meta Superintelligence Labs, built for real-world agentic work — Muse can turn your requests into plans, work through tasks across connected apps and websites, and keep working towards your goal. And with Muse, you’re in control. You choose what it can access, approve important actions before Muse carries them out , and can ask it to remember and or forget something. We built Muse to be private, safe, and secure by design. Every Muse gets its own virtual computer in the cloud, like a laptop that’s just for you. Your information and logins are kept there, not in Meta’s other services, and no one else’s Muse can access them. Muse works straight away, with no technical experience needed. Unlike other agents, Muse was built to work for billions of people worldwide, so there’s no learning curve. With your oversight, it can handle tasks like sending an email or booking travel, and taking on bigger goals: share one, and it will build a personalised plan, coordinate your time and resources, then advance the work itself – opening a browser, filling out forms, even chasing a refund negotiating on your behalf. And Muse can build a tracker, an itinerary, a study guide, a dashboard – describe the tool your life is missing and it will make it. For tasks that take more time, Muse keeps working after you close the app, coming back when something changes or it needs your approval, like before it sends an email or makes a purchase. It can get better results with less effort: selling a car for more, lowering a bill, adjusting a training plan when life shifts. When it comes time to pay, Muse can checkout with Link built by Stripe. Link’s wallet for agents generates a unique, digital version of your card that’s only accessible to agents using Link. This keeps your payment credentials safe and secure. Muse can also checkout with Shop Pay from Shopify with supported stores, which securely uses the payment and shipping details you’ve already saved with Shop Pay, so you can complete your purchase in just a few taps without entering them again. And Muse remembers what matters to you, so it can proactively make suggestions and act on details you’ve only mentioned once, like suggesting a menu for your dinner party before it sends the invites. We’ve set a high bar for these messages so they’re genuinely helpful and worth the interruption, and you can always tell your Muse to turn them off, dial them down or dial them up. No two Muses are alike. You give yours a name, a look and a personality, and it gets sharper the more you use it. Chat to it wherever suits you – in the Muse app or in WhatsApp – it’s your Muse wherever you call on it, with the same memory of how you like things done. You can also start side chats to keep different tasks organised, like planning a birthday in one and flat hunting in another. We’ve also introduced more ways to make Muse your own. With spaces, you can create your own custom experience inside Muse – like a tracker for your holiday savings, a weekly family planner or a board for your home renovation. Muse builds it, keeps it up to date, and you can pin it where you want in the app so what matters most is always within reach. Your Muse will also have its own voice for natural, real-time conversations. You can customise its voice by choosing from hundreds of options, including a range of British accents. Connectors are a big reason Muse can do so much for you. Connect your Instagram and Muse can help you turn a recipe Reel you’ve saved into a shopping list. Connect your email and calendar and it can help you sort your inbox, keep the family diary up to date and make sure nothing slips through the cracks. At launch, we’re also bringing dozens of our partners along, including global brands like Spotify and OpenTable. And to make Muse feel even more at home in the UK, we’re also working with UK connector partners such as Marks & Spencer, Debenhams Group, Currys, Ocado Retail, Trainline, Argos, Sainsbury’s, ASOS, Jet2, LOOKFANTASTIC, MyProtein, JustPark, easyJet and JD Sports. With some, you can connect your personal account so Muse can reorder your usual shop or pull up a booking. With others, Muse can find its way around their websites from day one, so it can help you find what you need and get it done. We’re also working to bring more brands into the Muse experience such as PayPal which is coming soon too. Over time, we’re working with these brands to bring new features to Muse, so they can do even more for you. Shruti Dube, UK Country Director at Meta: “I’m thrilled that millions of Brits will now have access to a personal agent that they control and that gets things done on their behalf. Partnering with beloved British brands and retailers means Muse works seamlessly with services people here use every day, making everything from the weekly shop to sorting out their travel needs easier.” You decide which Connectors your Muse can use, and how much access each one gets. You can add, or disconnect, a service whenever you want in your settings. To get things done, you can connect Muse to the apps you already use, from your email and calendar to the websites you shop on. We know that’s an act of trust, so you’re in control at every step: you decide which apps Muse connects to and what access it gets, you can see everything it’s done and plans to do next, and you can decide what it remembers. Above all, Muse asks for your go-ahead before important actions, like sending an email or making a purchase. Your conversations with Muse, and the data in your virtual machine, aren’t shared with Meta’s advertising systems. You also decide whether we can use your interactions with Muse to train and improve AI at Meta , and you can switch this off at any time in Settings. Muse has no visibility into people’s passwords or payment methods. To find out more about the controls you have, read Muse Does the Work, You Stay in Control on our Newsroom. And for more technical detail on how we built safety and control into Muse from the start, see How We Built Safety Into Muse . We think personal superintelligence will be one of the most transformative technologies of a lifetime. Muse is a first step: an agent that takes on more of the work, so people can focus on what matters to them. Muse is available to anyone aged 18 and over in the UK from today on iOS, Android, muse.ai and WhatsApp, and is coming to Meta’s AI glasses in the months ahead. It’s free to use for most of what people need, with subscription plans for those who want to do even more. We can’t wait to see what people across the UK get done with Muse.

Ant Group open-sources the AI behind its 150-million-user health app
Ant Group has released LingSante-3.1-flash and LingSante-3.1-air-VL on Hugging Face — medical models it says already power its 150-million-user Afu app. Ant Group has released the model weights of LingSante , the medical and health AI family that powers its health app Afu, to the public. The announcement, made on November 23, 2026, puts the weights of two core models on Hugging Face : LingSante-3.1-air-VL , a lightweight natively multimodal model with 124 billion total parameters and 5.5 billion active per token, and LingSante-3.1-flash , a 560-billion-parameter deep-reasoning model with roughly 25 billion active per token and a context window of up to one million tokens. The models are not lab experiments. They power Afu , a service that Ant says has reached 150 million users — up from 100 million in February 2026 — and handles nearly 20 million health consultations a day, making it one of the largest deployed health AI services anywhere. “The most profound impact of AI on healthcare is its ability to reshape how health services are delivered, making personalized care more accessible and affordable at scale,” said Cyril Han, CEO of Ant Group. “AI is becoming a bridge between clinical care in hospitals and health management beyond hospital settings.” LingSante-3.1-air-VL is built for consumer and small-institution use: it reads text, images and video natively, with capabilities in medical image understanding, skin-condition analysis, diet and nutrition assessment, and medical report interpretation. Its low active-parameter count allows deployment on workstation-class hardware such as NVIDIA RTX Spark-class devices — the company’s answer to the affordability problem that keeps specialist AI out of small clinics. LingSante-3.1-flash targets complex clinical reasoning, evidence-based retrieval and long-horizon workflow execution. Ant Group’s launch video for LingSante-3.1-flash. The company positions the model as a research tool, not a medical device. Video: Ant Group. Three specialized models round out the family: LingSante-Pulse, which assesses risk for more than 150 conditions from diverse health signals; LingSante-MedGuard , a dedicated safety model covering medical safety, regulatory compliance and bioethics; and LingSante-Live, a real-time multimodal agent already integrated into the Afu app for AI video consultations. For hospitals and clinics across Asia, the practical significance is deployment control. Open weights mean an institution can run the models on its own premises, keeping patient data inside its walls — and the lighter model’s efficiency makes that feasible without data-center budgets. The release also lands amid supportive policy: China’s five-department “AI + Healthcare” implementation opinion (October 2025) calls for building open-source medical AI software, with specialty models and agents targeted for use by 2027. On the consumer side, the app’s AI Health Manager already extends into roles such as weight-loss coach, nutritionist and parenting assistant, and connects with smart health devices across eight categories. Ant Group frames the release carefully. This is the company’s first open-sourced natively multimodal health model family — its earlier open medical model, Ling-3.0-flash-Santé (September 2026), was text-only — but the company does not claim to be first in open-source medical AI broadly. The models are positioned as a research and enabling tool: not a medical device, not a replacement for clinical diagnosis, and the imaging-report capability is explicitly research-only. MedGuard ships alongside to mitigate safety and compliance risks, and local deployment lets institutions operate within their own regulatory boundaries. The release sharpens a split in the medical AI market. Google’s MedGemma (4B/27B) remains the open research-first benchmark; OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s health offerings are closed-API. LingSante’s differentiator is production validation at consumer scale plus edge deployability. For institutions in the region weighing adoption, the open question is familiar: who is accountable when a model is wrong. Ant’s answer — on-premise deployment, a dedicated safety model, and a stated principle that AI assists doctors rather than replacing them — will be tested as the first real deployments begin.

Introducing Claude Ship
Open a pull request and get back to building. Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team's policy allows. Anyone who has opened a pull request knows how this goes. They start on the next thing, and then the review comes back. So they stop, dig back into the old code, push a fix, and wait for the review to run again. Then they go find someone to approve it. There's a good reason it works this way. Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that's easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now. On the Claude Code team, Claude writes most of our code , and we wanted everything after the PR to move that fast too. That's why we built Claude Ship , available today in beta. It can review PRs, fix them, and decide what's ready to merge based on policies each team sets. Teams stay in control of where it runs and which changes need a person. The goal: ship code as fast as teams write it. Claude Ship is made up of Code Review , which is already generally available, and two new agents in beta: PR Steward and Claude Approvals. Together, they take a pull request through review, fixes, and an approval decision so teams don't have to manage each step manually. Code Review performs an in-depth review of pull requests against the codebase through multiple lenses. It collects findings, adversarially verifies them, categorizes them, and posts them to a PR. On the Claude Code team, where Claude's review is one layer of a broader process, merged PRs more than doubled from June to September while the share reverted fell by more than 40%. Code Review gives teams fast reviews, clear findings, and a choice of Quick, Standard, or Deep review levels for each repository. PR Steward works to keep a PR green, but is designed not to approve or merge pull requests. It jumps in on failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback from Code Review, other review tools, or team members. After every push, it comments with what it changed and how to undo it. Developers can comment @claude with an instruction to steer the work, or @claude stop to have it step back. From there, Claude Approvals applies an approval policy that the team writes as a file in the repository. Claude can approve routine changes on its own if the policy allows it, or can require deeper human sign-off for certain scenarios. It works like a smarter CODEOWNERS file. Teams can have Claude Approvals consider a variety of signals in its decision-making process, including Code Review findings or their own classifiers using natural language. For most customers, we recommend enabling this first in observe-only mode to build confidence before configuring branch protection to require Claude Approvals' green light. Developers can try Claude Ship on their own pull requests with the new /ship command in Claude Code. When a change is ready, they run /ship . Claude pushes it, opens the PR, reviews the change, and works on feedback and failing checks to help get it ready to merge. What can merge depends on the developer's permissions and the repository's branch rules. Turning Claude Ship on for an entire repository puts it to work across a team's pull requests automatically, under settings and an approval policy the team controls. Developers don't need to manually invoke the /ship command. Teams set the pace. They can start with one repository, choose a review level and when reviews run, set a monthly spend limit, and run their approval policy in observe mode until they trust it. We run Claude Ship on many of our own pull requests. One of the biggest changes is who can act on customer feedback.
